authProtocolScope: Official Stellar SDK SEP-10 challenge building and threshold verification, followed by Atlas-local opaque bearer sessions. These endpoints do not implement a SEP-10 JWT/discovery server and must not be advertised as one.

configuration.ATLAS_VERIFICATION_ENABLED: Explicit true only after source, native database, build and operational admission. Omitted/false keeps HTTP authentication and verification writes disabled.
configuration.ATLAS_VERIFICATION_ORIGIN: Exact canonical HTTPS origin of the app, with no port or trailing slash; DNS hostname at most 58 characters.
configuration.ATLAS_VERIFICATION_HOME_DOMAIN: Optional; must equal the configured origin hostname. Defaults to that hostname.
configuration.ATLAS_VERIFICATION_SERVER_SEED_FILE: The only supported value is /etc/stellaratlas/account-verification/server.seed, an existing operator-provisioned dedicated signing file. All ancestors must be ordinary root-owned directories without group/other write permission; the file must be a nonempty ordinary single-link file of at most 128 bytes, owned by root or the service user, with no group/other permissions. Symlinks, arbitrary paths and credential fallback are rejected. File validation and the bounded read use the same opened descriptor, with no pre-open leaf pathname check. This source selection does not create the directory, file or key; provisioning, readable service-user ownership and activation require separate operator admission. No key is generated by the application.
configuration.ATLAS_VERIFICATION_SERVER_ACCOUNT: The explicitly selected public G address matching that seed. Publish/verify this signing account through the existing Atlas domain configuration for wallet challenge verification; do not overwrite unrelated TOML settings.
configuration.ATLAS_VERIFICATION_HORIZON_MAINNET_URL: Explicit operator-trusted mainnet Horizon base URL, HTTPS or literal loopback HTTP. At least one network endpoint is required.
configuration.ATLAS_VERIFICATION_HORIZON_TESTNET_URL: Optional explicit testnet Horizon base URL under the same transport policy. Each endpoint must report the exact SDK network passphrase, provide the account Latest-Ledger header, complete signer/threshold evidence and that ledger's close time within 30 seconds.
configuration.ATLAS_VERIFICATION_REVIEWERS: JSON array of 1 to 16 distinct objects with exactly network and address fields. Each G account must be explicitly operator-selected and on a configured network. Authentication server account is ineligible. No default principal, email/scanner credentials, client role or imported identity grants reviewer permission.

schemaAdmission.procedure: Keep DATABASE_MIGRATIONS_RUN disabled for normal serving. Qualify/admit these exact additive migrations via the existing migration release procedure. Running all pending migrations requires review of that entire pending set; the verification feature flag does not suppress DDL.
schemaAdmission.roles: Use the existing application database connection and explicitly admit access to these feature tables. Source delivery does not grant or apply production database privileges.

supportedAccounts: Existing classic G accounts with Ed25519 signer entries, including weighted multisig. Required signature weight is max(1, low, medium, high threshold). Nonexistent, muxed/memo-scoped, contract, non-Ed25519 signer and authentication-server-as-signer cases do not qualify.

authentication.challenge: POST /v1/account-verification/auth/challenge with network and address; SDK random nonce, sequence zero, configured home/web-auth domain, exact five-minute bounds and durable issued transaction hash.
authentication.exchange: POST /v1/account-verification/auth/session with network and wallet-signed transaction; all signatures accounted for by the SDK against current weighted signers; atomic one-time challenge consumption before a session is returned.
authentication.session: 256-bit random opaque bearer, only SHA256 hash retained, expires with the original challenge (at most five minutes), browser memory only, no ambient cookie authentication. Current account authority is rechecked for every authenticated HTTP request and deduplicated within that request.
authentication.logout: DELETE /v1/account-verification/auth/session with the bearer token revokes the session. Existing submitted claims remain for review.
authentication.reviewContinuity: For at most 24 hours, retain the signer set whose challenge signatures were verified. An allowlisted reviewer may reassess that original proof against fresh current account weights/thresholds for the exact applicant/network/address. This is continuity of the earlier authenticated proof, not a new wallet signature at review time. Expired/insufficient proof requires a new applicant challenge and resubmission.
authentication.identity: Account authority never establishes the claimed organization identity; approval still requires the independent Atlas reviewer decision and explicit identity-evidence assessment.

beforeActivation: Independent review of the signed successor, including the native TypeORM result normalization correction; do not deploy the earlier cc3edb03 source by itself.
Use the retained disposable native PostgreSQL fixture to qualify the corrected application update and new authentication migration, atomic challenge consumption, replay and session admission paths.

Release builds the exact reviewed source, admits the exact schema and selected operational inputs, verifies one configured network and clock freshness, then enables through the existing reversible release path.
Browser-check the manual wallet XDR sign-in, private submission/status flow and sign-out on that build. Never request a wallet seed or broadcast the authentication transaction.
Complete the reviewer UI and bind approved Atlas identities into account/search presentation as remaining product work. Imports remain independently attributed.
